prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one single 9:16 vertical static story plate for an original cruise-ship mystery. Three provided images are the ONLY visual STYLE references: bold heavy black 2D graphic-novel ink, flat cel-shaded shapes, restrained cool slate contrast, clean hard rim light. Do not copy their scenes, characters, faces, signs, lighting fixtures or rain. Entire ship, props and figures share an inked 2D comic medium, no glossy photorealistic 3D, no soft webtoon/manhwa shading. Survivor is a compact adult, gender-neutral, wearing a dark hood-raised windbreaker, straight cargo trousers, and rubber-soled shoes. Nonhuman entity is notably taller and slender with a bald smooth dark head, rigid unnatural head/shoulders and tense long fingers; matte #07080B except two extremely small pale pinpoint eye glints. Both figures are solid matte #07080B with crisp practical edge-light; survivor has zero visible facial features, skin tone or shaded hands. Use coherent anatomy and no duplicated figures. When floor and full body are visible, include EVERY figure head to whole foot with clear space around shoes. Empty POV — no foreground duplicate character. One time, one camera view, no inset, split screen, text overlay or watermark. No baked-in rain, mist, storm streaks, lightning, flash, camera roll, impact effects, sparks, motion blur, shake, speed lines, glitch, or titles. Static wet deck puddles and sea water are allowed; Remotion will add timed effects. Composition and camera viewpoint remain clean and neutral.

Exact location anchor: An outdoor, three-metre-wide exterior passenger corridor on Deck 6 of a cruise ship at night. Viewed lengthwise along the corridor, the ship's dull off-white steel inner bulkhead with closed round portholes and a closed horizontal sliding cabin door is on the left; a thick rusty storm chain and padlock secure that door from the exterior. A row of orange life jackets hangs on individual wall hooks beside the door. On the right is a chest-high dark steel safety railing above the open black sea. An orange-dark rescue lifeboat hangs overhead from a steel davit, with its cable leading to a manual brake lever and separate locking bar stored on a bracket near the davit base. The steel deck is textured tread plate with shallow static puddles. Cool slate/cyan ship light and restrained warm sodium practical light illuminate the scene. The deck and props use a single cohesive hand-inked 2D graphic-noir medium. The sea and sky are outdoors. No painted falling rain, sea mist, lightning, flash, camera shake, rolling, motion trails, title or text overlay; transient effects are supplied later in Remotion.

P19: A tight FRONT-ON image of the WALL CONTACT MOMENT, camera perpendicular to the vertical steel bulkhead. The massive orange lifeboat hull presses the ONE black nonhuman entity against the inner bulkhead, blocking its lower torso from view. Its one head with TWO tiny pale eye glints and its chest are visible above the top edge of the orange hull. The trapped entity REVEALS FOUR ARMS AND FOUR SEPARATE HANDS, all four fully visible above the boat, splayed against the wall: one upper arm and one lower arm extend left from its torso, and one upper arm and one lower arm extend right. Exactly one head, two eyes, four arms, four hands, one torso. All arms clearly connect to the same upper body. The bulkhead is the vertical side wall of an exterior corridor, not a new end wall. The ocean and rail are out of this close crop. No other figures, no gore, blood, writing, flash, rain, smoke, camera shake, blur, or motion lines. Cool steel slate and ink black; restrained sodium rim light. One static moment.
